prompts:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: wide watercolor landscape background for a wedding invitation.
Input 1 EDIT TARGET: approved nighttime chapel panorama. Input 2 MANDATORY STYLE MASTER: watercolor bottle/lemons, medium and muted palette only. Input 3 APPROVED INVITATION SCENE: softness, painted texture and visual consistency only.
Edit ONLY the LANDSCAPE BELOW THE NIGHT SKY, on the RIGHT THIRD where the little domed chapel stands. Replace the chapel with an elegant romantic Italian mountain hotel / historic alpine lakeside villa: three or four stories, many welcoming warmly lit windows, gracefully repeated balconies, pale cream stucco and natural stone, soft muted roof, cypress and mountain gardens. Keep the hotel centered in exactly the position of the chapel at 75% of canvas width; building and garden in bottom 40%, roof no higher than about 60% of canvas height. Make hotel somewhat wider than chapel, comfortably filling the portrait viewport in right third. Preserve the lake and Italian mountains around it, terrace perspective, luminous cobblestone approach and vegetation in the same soft traditional watercolor. No chapel dome or cross, no hotel name, no people, no text, no modern signs.
ABSOLUTELY PRESERVE THE ENTIRE TOP HALF OF THE IMAGE: SAME NAVY WATERCOLOR SKY, SAME MOON POSITION/SIZE, SAME EXISTING STARS, SAME COLOR, SAME TEXTURE, SAME CANVAS/COMPOSITION. It must connect perfectly with the preceding shot of this exact sky. Do not add or move a moon. Do not zoom or reframe. Keep wide original aspect ratio ~2.288:1 and original arrangement outside the right-side architecture.
Style: hand-painted soft watercolor pigment/paper texture within the painting, muted navy night, pale sky blue, warm butter-yellow windows, ivory walls, desaturated olive/sage foliage, delicate organic loose brushwork. NO photorealism, NO vector outlines, NO 3D, NO plastic, NO saturated orange or violet. High-quality elegant composition, natural proportions, no blur. Opaque landscape, not transparent.

Precise composition correction. Input 1 is the hotel illustration to edit. Input 2 is the original night chapel panorama with the EXACT protected sky. Input 3 watercolor master and input 4 approved invitation watercolor style.
Keep the hotel design, nighttime lighting and all watercolor style. IMPORTANT: move the hotel and its tall flanking trees DOWN into the lower 40 percent of the panorama, slightly reduce their size uniformly so there is generous uninterrupted night sky above. On the 1897 by 829 image, the hotel roof and chimneys must begin at y=490 or below, the hotel facade should end around y=710, hotel center x=1422. The hotel should have three stories with many balconies and warm windows, still naturally proportioned. Its tallest immediately adjacent cypress trees must begin below y=440. Keep cobbled foreground, mountain/lake atmosphere, ivory stone and gardens in the bottom. Restore every pixel of sky above y=416 from input 2 with exactly the same moon and stars in their original locations. No architecture or tree silhouettes in that upper half. Do not move the moon, do not add another moon, no texts/logos/people. Preserve overall wide 2.288:1 canvas. The center of interest is the right third as before. Soft traditional watercolor as the mandatory master: muted navy/sky blue, butter yellow lights, cream stone, desaturated olive greenery. No vector, black outlines, 3D, photo or saturated violet.
integration: Original night sky remains underneath. A CSS alpha mask reveals the hotel panorama only below y=416 in a 1897×829 world. The same sky, moon and additional star layer remain continuous during descent and reverse ascent.
